page_header: Breathing and Exchange of Gases · 4 marks

steps.label: Asthma
steps.why: Asthma is an inflammation of the airways, so the air passage narrows and the difficulty is in moving air, not in absorbing it.
common_mistakes: Calling asthma an infection. It is an inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles.
Leaving out the symptoms. Wheezing is the marking word.
steps.memory_tip: Asthma narrows the tubes, so the breath whistles.
steps.margin_note: Open by listing all five, then take them one by one.

steps.label: Bronchitis, emphysema
steps.why: In emphysema the alveolar walls break down, so the surface for gas exchange is lost for good and the damage cannot be repaired.
common_mistakes: Writing that emphysema can be cured. The alveolar lining is damaged beyond repair.
Confusing the two. Bronchitis is in the tubes, emphysema is in the alveoli.
steps.memory_tip: Bronchitis is mucus in the tubes; emphysema is broken alveoli.
steps.margin_note: One or two lines each. Name smoking as the cause.

steps.label: Pneumonia
steps.why: Pneumonia is the one infection in the list, so the answer must name an organism as well as the effect on the alveoli.
common_mistakes: Giving no causal organism. Streptococcus pneumoniae is the marking name.
Describing it as an airway narrowing. The alveoli fill with fluid.
steps.memory_tip: Pneumonia is an infection, so the alveoli fill with fluid.
steps.margin_note: Name the organism, then the symptoms.

steps.label: Occupational disorders
steps.why: These four are caused by dust that the body cannot clear, so the disease follows the job rather than any infection.
common_mistakes: Naming the disease without the industry. The pair is what is marked.
Writing silicosis for coal miners. Coal dust causes black lung disease.
steps.memory_tip: Asbestos, silica, iron, coal — asbestosis, silicosis, siderosis, black lung.
steps.margin_note: Write these four as a list with the industry beside each.
lines: Long exposure to dust in certain industries
4. Black lung disease — coal mine workers.

insider_note: This question is asked more often than any other four-mark question in the chapter. Name all five groups first — a student who describes only asthma and pneumonia caps the answer at two marks.
